meta.status: Draft for Steven's review. Question wording, trigger criteria and the selection rules are proposals, not verified.

selection_rules._status: Proposals. Values marked [unverified] in the repo (FUP-TGT-004) stay proposals until Steven rules.
selection_rules.order_of_interview: shared opening, then the five role core questions in order, then shared closing
selection_rules.core_questions: Always asked, in order, exactly as written unless the user asks for a repeat or hint (INT-CTL-001, INT-CTL-002).
selection_rules.followups: Asked only when the decider chooses probe (FUP-DEC-001) and a trigger fires on the answer text. Each follow-up's focus is the short phrase for FUP-DEC-002.
selection_rules.choosing_between_triggers: If several fire, ask the lowest priority number first. If tied, prefer a depth trigger over a content trigger. Stop at the cap.
selection_rules.role_followup_vs_generic: Use the role follow-up whose trigger fired. If none applies, use the shared generic follow-up for that trigger as a fallback.
never_probe_when: The answer is empty or says the person does not know (FUP-DEC-005)
The transcript confidence is too low to trust the content (FUP-DEC-006)
The probe cap has been reached (FUP-DEC-004)
selection_rules.grounding: Bank text is role-level and works in Cold interviews. In Hot interviews the interviewer model may add resume-grounded questions on top, but must not claim facts that are not in the resume or the answers (INT-CTX-002).
selection_rules.paraphrasing: Follow-up text is the default, speakable version. The interviewer may paraphrase it to fit the answer (INT-FUP-001) while keeping one question, two sentences at most.

tts_rules: One ask per utterance: a single question, or a single spoken request such as 'tell me about a time...'. At most two sentences (INT-ONE-001, INT-LEN-001).
Plain letters only: no digits, symbols, slashes, parentheses, quotes, colons or markdown (INT-STR-002).
Numbers are written as words. Capitalised acronyms must be in the pronunciation map.
Core questions up to 28 words, follow-ups up to 24 words, so a turn is about 10 seconds or less when spoken.
Nothing depends on sight or sound (no 'as you can see', 'click', 'on screen').
Nothing asks about protected characteristics or health (INT-CND-002).
never_trigger_on: How fast or slow the person speaks, pauses, long silences, or hesitation
Stuttering, repeated words, or false starts
Grammar, spelling, vocabulary level, or writing style
Audio quality, clipped audio, or a low-confidence transcript (FUP-DEC-006)
Whether the answer was spoken or typed, or whether captions, hints, repeats, push-to-talk or 'give me a sec' were used (EVL-FAI-001)
Anything about age, family, health, disability, religion, nationality or other protected characteristics (INT-CND-002)

no_specific_example.definition: The question asked about a real past situation, but the answer stays general or hypothetical and names no concrete occasion.

no_outcome.definition: The answer describes what the candidate did but never says how it ended or what changed.

no_personal_role.definition: The answer describes what a team or group did, and the candidate's own part is unclear.

no_measure.definition: The answer describes a result or scale but gives no size, amount, frequency or other measure, where a measure would naturally exist. Use sparingly.

unclear_answer.definition: The CONTENT of the answer is ambiguous or seems to contradict itself. Never because of audio, transcript quality, fluency or wording style (FUP-DEC-006).

mentions_conflict.definition: The answer mentions a disagreement, a difficult person, or a clash of priorities.

mentions_mistake.definition: The answer mentions an error, failure, miss or problem, theirs or someone else's.

mentions_tool_or_method.definition: The answer names a specific tool, system, technique, process or credential.

mentions_leadership.definition: The answer mentions guiding, training, coaching, delegating to or influencing others.

mentions_time_pressure.definition: The answer mentions a tight deadline, heavy workload, or competing demands.

mentions_improvement.definition: The answer mentions changing, fixing or improving a process, product or situation.

mentions_customer.definition: The answer mentions a customer, client, patient, guest, vendor, or other person being served.

skips_safety_or_compliance_step.definition: The answer describes a shortcut, or leaves out a safety, accuracy, privacy, quality or compliance check that this role would normally require.

strong_answer_stretch.definition: The answer is complete, specific and shows clear results. Ask one harder variation to test depth.

core_categories.motivation: Why this kind of work or role; keeps the interviewer grounded in the role.
core_categories.experience: A real past example of doing the core work of the role.
core_categories.behavioral: A real past example of a people or pressure situation common in the role.
core_categories.scenario: A realistic role-specific situation the candidate talks through (may be hypothetical).
core_categories.growth: Learning, strengths or development, framed for the role.
